name: Next.js
description: Senior interview preparation for modern Next.js App Router applications, aligned with Next.js 16.x behavior: rendering, Server and Client Components, Cache Components, data fetching, revalidation, Route Handlers, Server Actions, navigation, performance, and production/self-hosting concerns.

questions.question: What is the App Router in modern Next.js?
options: A file-system router built around React features such as Server Components, Suspense, and Server Functions
A client-only router that requires React Router
A router available only for static exports
questions.answer: A file-system router built around React features such as Server Components, Suspense, and Server Functions
questions.explanation: The App Router is file-system based and integrates modern React server rendering, streaming, and mutation primitives.

questions.question: In the App Router, what are page.tsx and layout.tsx components by default?
questions.answer: Server Components
questions.explanation: Pages and layouts are Server Components by default; client behavior is introduced explicitly where needed.

questions.question: Which requirements normally indicate that a component should be a Client Component?
options: It uses useState or event handlers
It performs a server-side SQL query
answers: It uses useState or event handlers
questions.explanation: Client Components are appropriate for state, effects, event handlers, and browser-only APIs.

questions.question: What does adding 'use client' at the top of a module do?
options: Creates a boundary where that module and its imports become part of the client module graph
Makes only the first function run in the browser
Forces the whole application into CSR
questions.answer: Creates a boundary where that module and its imports become part of the client module graph
questions.explanation: The directive defines the server/client module boundary; it does not need to be repeated in every descendant.

questions.question: Adding 'use client' to a high-level component can increase the amount of JavaScript shipped to the browser.
questions.explanation: Its imported dependency tree can enter the client bundle, so narrow client boundaries generally reduce shipped JavaScript.

questions.question: Props passed from a Server Component to a Client Component generally need to be what?
questions.answer: Serializable by React
questions.explanation: Values crossing the server/client boundary must be serializable by React.

questions.question: What is a major benefit of querying a database directly from a Server Component?
options: Credentials and query logic can remain on the server without an extra browser-facing API hop
questions.answer: Credentials and query logic can remain on the server without an extra browser-facing API hop
questions.explanation: Server Components can access server resources directly, but authentication and authorization are still required.

questions.question: Because a Server Component runs on the server, authorization checks can be skipped for its database queries.
questions.explanation: Server-side execution protects implementation details and credentials, not access control.

questions.question: What is the React Server Component Payload used for?
options: Representing rendered Server Components plus references/placeholders for Client Components
Replacing HTML on the initial request
questions.answer: Representing rendered Server Components plus references/placeholders for Client Components
questions.explanation: The RSC payload lets React reconcile the Server and Client Component trees during initial load and navigation.

questions.question: On the initial load of a route containing Client Components, which description is most accurate?
options: HTML shows an immediate preview, the RSC payload reconciles the trees, and JavaScript hydrates Client Components
Only the RSC payload is sent
Server Components are hydrated with useEffect
questions.answer: HTML shows an immediate preview, the RSC payload reconciles the trees, and JavaScript hydrates Client Components
questions.explanation: Initial rendering combines server-generated HTML, the RSC payload, and Client Component JavaScript.

questions.question: In App Router terminology, what best corresponds to traditional SSG?
options: Prerendering at build time or during revalidation and serving a cached result
Running a Route Handler for every paint
questions.answer: Prerendering at build time or during revalidation and serving a cached result
questions.explanation: Modern Next.js documentation describes this mainly as prerendering/static rendering.

questions.question: In App Router terminology, what best corresponds to request-time SSR?
options: Dynamic Rendering on the server in response to a request
questions.answer: Dynamic Rendering on the server in response to a request
questions.explanation: Dynamic rendering generates route output at request time.

questions.question: In current Next.js 16 behavior, what is the default persistent caching behavior of fetch() in Server Components?
options: fetch responses are not cached by default
questions.answer: fetch responses are not cached by default
questions.explanation: Current Next.js documentation states that fetch requests are uncached by default; explicit caching is opt-in.

questions.question: What happens to identical fetch requests made in the same React component tree?
options: They can be memoized/deduplicated during rendering
They are cached forever across requests
questions.answer: They can be memoized/deduplicated during rendering
questions.explanation: Render-time request memoization is distinct from persistent caching across requests.

questions.question: Render-time memoization of identical fetch calls is the same as persistent server caching across user requests.
questions.explanation: Deduplicating work during one render and retaining results across requests are different mechanisms.

questions.question: What must be enabled to use the Next.js 16 Cache Components model?
questions.answer: cacheComponents: true in next.config
questions.explanation: Cache Components and the 'use cache' directive are enabled with the cacheComponents option.

questions.question: Where can the 'use cache' directive be applied?
options: At file, async component, or async function level
questions.answer: At file, async component, or async function level
questions.explanation: 'use cache' can cache a route/file scope, component output, or asynchronous function result.

questions.question: What does cacheLife() control inside a 'use cache' scope?
questions.answer: Cache freshness/lifetime semantics
questions.explanation: cacheLife selects or configures how cached data ages and revalidates.

questions.question: What is cacheTag() used for?
options: Associating cached work with tags that can later be invalidated
questions.answer: Associating cached work with tags that can later be invalidated
questions.explanation: Tags let mutations invalidate data shared across routes without coupling to a single URL.

questions.question: In Next.js 16, when is updateTag() especially appropriate?
options: After a user mutation when immediate read-your-writes behavior is needed
questions.answer: After a user mutation when immediate read-your-writes behavior is needed
questions.explanation: updateTag is designed for mutations where the user should immediately see their own updated data.

questions.question: What is the recommended modern behavior of revalidateTag(tag, 'max')?
options: Mark tagged data stale and use stale-while-revalidate on the next visit
Delete the entire app cache immediately
questions.answer: Mark tagged data stale and use stale-while-revalidate on the next visit
questions.explanation: The 'max' profile serves stale data while refreshing in the background when the tagged resource is next visited.

questions.question: What does revalidatePath() invalidate?
options: Cached data associated with a specific path
questions.answer: Cached data associated with a specific path
questions.explanation: revalidatePath is path-oriented; tag APIs are useful when the same data appears across multiple paths.

questions.question: Calling refresh() from a Server Action automatically invalidates all tagged server cache entries.
questions.explanation: refresh() refreshes the client router; cache invalidation still uses updateTag, revalidateTag, or revalidatePath.

questions.question: What is the status of unstable_cache in Next.js 16?
options: It has been superseded by 'use cache' in the Cache Components model
It is the only supported cache API
It is mandatory for Route Handlers
questions.answer: It has been superseded by 'use cache' in the Cache Components model
questions.explanation: Next.js 16 recommends moving Cache Components workloads from unstable_cache to 'use cache'.

questions.question: Why should cookies() or headers() normally be read outside a standard 'use cache' scope and passed in as arguments?
options: They are request-specific runtime data and should be explicit inputs to cached work
They work only in Client Components
questions.answer: They are request-specific runtime data and should be explicit inputs to cached work
questions.explanation: Cached functions should have deterministic inputs; request-specific values are normally read outside the cached scope.

questions.question: What is true of cookies() and headers() in current Next.js?
questions.answer: They are asynchronous APIs
questions.explanation: Modern Next.js exposes these request APIs asynchronously.

questions.question: Where can cookies be written using the Next.js cookies API?
questions.answer: Server Functions/Actions or Route Handlers
questions.explanation: Server Components can read incoming cookies, while outgoing cookie mutation belongs in mutation/request-handler contexts.

questions.question: Where are App Router Route Handlers defined?
options: In route.ts or route.js files under app
questions.answer: In route.ts or route.js files under app
questions.explanation: Route Handlers use the Web Request and Response APIs and are the App Router request-handler convention.

questions.question: Which HTTP methods can a Route Handler export?
questions.explanation: Supported methods include GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, and OPTIONS.

questions.question: A page.tsx and route.ts can both exist at the same route segment and handle the same path.
questions.explanation: They conflict at the same route level because each takes over the route.

questions.question: What is the default caching behavior of Route Handlers in current Next.js?
options: They are not cached by default; GET can explicitly opt into static caching
questions.answer: They are not cached by default; GET can explicitly opt into static caching
questions.explanation: GET handlers can opt into static behavior, while other HTTP methods remain dynamic.

questions.question: A Server Component needs data from the same application's database. Why is calling your own Route Handler usually unnecessary?
options: It can call the data layer directly and avoid an extra server HTTP request
questions.answer: It can call the data layer directly and avoid an extra server HTTP request
questions.explanation: Route Handlers are useful network boundaries, but Server Components can usually access server-side data sources directly.

questions.question: What is a Server Function?
options: An asynchronous function that executes on the server and can be invoked from application code
Any function inside a Server Component
questions.answer: An asynchronous function that executes on the server and can be invoked from application code
questions.explanation: A Server Action is a Server Function used in an action/mutation context.

questions.question: Which directive marks a function or module as containing Server Functions?
questions.answer: 'use server'
questions.explanation: The directive can be used in an async function body or at module level.

questions.question: A Server Function can be defined directly inside a Client Component.
questions.explanation: Client Components can invoke imported Server Functions, but cannot define them directly.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is used behind the scenes to invoke Server Actions?
questions.answer: POST
questions.explanation: Server Actions are mutation-oriented and are invoked through POST.

questions.question: Forms invoking Server Actions can support progressive enhancement when JavaScript has not loaded.
questions.explanation: Server Action forms can submit without client JavaScript, improving resilience.

questions.question: What should a Server Action do with client-provided identifiers and form fields before a privileged mutation?
options: Validate input and perform server-side authentication/authorization
Trust them because Actions are private
questions.answer: Validate input and perform server-side authentication/authorization
questions.explanation: Treat Server Actions as server endpoints: their arguments are untrusted and authorization must be enforced server-side.

questions.question: How do you declare a basic dynamic App Router segment named slug?
questions.answer: [slug]
questions.explanation: A directory such as app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx creates a dynamic route segment.

questions.question: In current Next.js, what type of value is the params prop for an async dynamic page?
options: A Promise that should be awaited
questions.answer: A Promise that should be awaited
questions.explanation: Current route APIs expose params asynchronously; older versions permitted synchronous access.

questions.question: What is generateStaticParams() used for?
options: Providing dynamic route parameter values to prerender at build time
questions.answer: Providing dynamic route parameter values to prerender at build time
questions.explanation: It can prerender all or a selected subset of known dynamic paths.

questions.question: What does a folder named [...slug] represent?
questions.answer: A catch-all dynamic segment
questions.explanation: Catch-all segments capture multiple path segments into one parameter.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of loading.tsx in an App Router segment?
options: Provide an immediate Suspense fallback while route content streams
questions.answer: Provide an immediate Suspense fallback while route content streams
questions.explanation: Next.js automatically places a Suspense boundary around the relevant page content.

questions.question: What are benefits of appropriately placed Suspense boundaries?
options: Users can see fallback UI earlier
Fast content need not wait for the slowest data source
answers: Users can see fallback UI earlier
Fast content need not wait for the slowest data source
questions.explanation: Suspense improves rendering and streaming behavior; it is not a persistent cache.

questions.question: Two independent database requests are awaited one after another in the same Server Component. What problem can this create?
questions.answer: A request waterfall
questions.explanation: Independent operations should often be initiated concurrently rather than serialized.

questions.question: When several independent requests must all complete before rendering, what is a common way to start them concurrently?
questions.answer: Promise.all()
questions.explanation: Parallel initiation reduces avoidable sequential latency.

questions.question: What does Next.js Link provide for internal navigation?
options: Prefetching and client-side transitions while preserving shared UI where possible
A Server Action for every click
questions.answer: Prefetching and client-side transitions while preserving shared UI where possible
questions.explanation: Link integrates with the App Router to make server-rendered routes navigate with SPA-like responsiveness.

questions.question: How does standard automatic prefetching differ for static and dynamic routes?
options: Static routes can be fully prefetched; dynamic routes may be skipped or partially prefetched when loading UI is available
Dynamic routes are always fully prefetched
questions.answer: Static routes can be fully prefetched; dynamic routes may be skipped or partially prefetched when loading UI is available
questions.explanation: loading.tsx can provide a useful prefetched shell for otherwise request-time dynamic routes.

questions.question: Why can adding loading.tsx improve perceived navigation performance for a dynamic route?
options: It enables immediate fallback UI and streaming instead of leaving the user waiting for the full server response
questions.answer: It enables immediate fallback UI and streaming instead of leaving the user waiting for the full server response
questions.explanation: The route can transition immediately to a loading state while slower content arrives.

questions.question: When might `<Link prefetch={false}>` be reasonable?
options: For very large or low-probability link collections where background prefetching wastes resources
Whenever a route has a layout
questions.answer: For very large or low-probability link collections where background prefetching wastes resources
questions.explanation: Prefetching trades background work for lower navigation latency.

questions.question: What does next/image primarily help optimize?
options: Responsive sizing, lazy loading, layout stability, and modern image delivery
questions.answer: Responsive sizing, lazy loading, layout stability, and modern image delivery
questions.explanation: The Image component supplies framework-level image optimization and loading behavior.

questions.question: Starting with Next.js 16, which prop is preferred over the deprecated next/image priority prop when an image should be preloaded?
questions.answer: preload
questions.explanation: Next.js 16 deprecated priority in favor of the more explicit preload prop.

questions.question: What is a major performance/privacy benefit of next/font?
options: It self-hosts and optimizes fonts without requiring runtime requests to an external font provider
It converts fonts to React components
questions.answer: It self-hosts and optimizes fonts without requiring runtime requests to an external font provider
questions.explanation: Self-hosting reduces external requests and helps avoid font-related layout shifts.

questions.question: A page's client JavaScript bundle is unexpectedly large and hydration/prefetch starts late. What is a high-value investigation?
options: Inspect bundle composition and narrow 'use client' boundaries or move work back to the server
Convert every component to a Client Component
questions.answer: Inspect bundle composition and narrow 'use client' boundaries or move work back to the server
questions.explanation: Large client bundles delay download, parsing, hydration, and route prefetch behavior.

questions.question: Which App Router mechanisms are intended for page metadata?
options: A static metadata export or generateMetadata(), plus supported metadata files
questions.answer: A static metadata export or generateMetadata(), plus supported metadata files
questions.explanation: Next.js supports both configuration-based and file-based metadata conventions.

questions.question: What does a route group such as app/(marketing)/about/page.tsx do to the URL?
options: It organizes routes without adding '(marketing)' to the URL
questions.answer: It organizes routes without adding '(marketing)' to the URL
questions.explanation: Route groups affect organization/layout structure, not the pathname.

questions.question: What does error.tsx primarily provide in the App Router?
options: An error-boundary UI for uncaught runtime errors in a route segment
questions.answer: An error-boundary UI for uncaught runtime errors in a route segment
questions.explanation: Special error files let App Router segments isolate failures and render recovery UI.

questions.question: In Next.js 16, what happened to the middleware.ts convention?
options: It was deprecated in favor of proxy.ts for the network-boundary use case
questions.answer: It was deprecated in favor of proxy.ts for the network-boundary use case
questions.explanation: The rename clarifies that the feature operates at a routing/network boundary rather than as general application middleware.

questions.question: A self-hosted Next.js application runs on four ECS tasks. Why can relying only on a default instance-local cache cause inconsistent behavior?
options: Each Next.js process can have its own cache and different requests may hit different tasks
Server Components cannot be cached in containers
questions.answer: Each Next.js process can have its own cache and different requests may hit different tasks
questions.explanation: Horizontal self-hosting requires deliberate cache coordination when cache state must be shared across processes.

questions.question: What is a reason to configure a shared/custom Next.js cache handler in a multi-instance deployment?
options: To share cache state across instances or persist it beyond an individual process lifetime
To make Client Components execute on the server
questions.answer: To share cache state across instances or persist it beyond an individual process lifetime
questions.explanation: A distributed or durable cache can coordinate cached work across containers when the default local cache is insufficient.
